request.system:
You explain a fitted credit-risk model to a credit risk manager who is not a data scientist. You receive the facts about one model and write a short explanation of what drives its predictions of default.

# The text

- Write 5 to 8 sentences in plain English, most important drivers first.
- Mention an interaction when it matters for the model's predictions.
- Say only what the facts support. Do not round a weak effect up to a strong one, and do not add knowledge about credit risk that the facts do not show.
- When the facts do not settle something, say so ("the data do not settle whether ...") or leave it out.

# The answer

Return one JSON object with one list, `sentences`, each with an `id` (1, 2, 3, ...) and its `text`.
messages:
These are the facts about the model.

Model: a gradient-boosted tree model of depth 2 (XGB2), fitted to predict whether a credit applicant defaults (30,000 applicants). Effects are on the log-odds scale: positive values raise the risk of default. Every band is a 95% band from 100 refits of the model on resampled data.

Features, in the order of their share of the model's importance:
- `PAY_0`: repayment status in September 2005, the latest month (-1 paid in full, 1 to 9 months of payment delay; -2 and 0 are not in the data dictionary, commonly read as no consumption and revolving credit used).
  Share of importance 34.7% (95% band 31.3% to 43.9%); rank 1 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= -1: -0.2; 0: -0.5; 1: +0.7; >= 2: +2.3 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +2.44, 95% band [+2.36, +2.68]).
- `LIMIT_BAL`: amount of the given credit in NT dollars, individual and family (supplementary) credit.
  Share of importance 18.9% (95% band 16.1% to 22.0%); rank 2 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 79999: +0.5; 80000-159999: 0; >= 160000: -0.36 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -1.13, 95% band [-1.30, -0.83]).
- `PAY_AMT1`: amount paid in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 8.9% (95% band 6.3% to 11.1%); rank 3 to 4 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 2104: +0.139; >= 2105: -0.16 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.57, 95% band [-0.69, -0.32]).
- `BILL_AMT1`: amount of the bill statement in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 8.0% (95% band 3.5% to 9.7%); rank 3 to 5 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 5445: -0.195; >= 5446: +0.04 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.64, 95% band [+0.29, +0.81]).
- `PAY_AMT2`: amount paid in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 5.1% (95% band 2.2% to 7.4%); rank 3 to 6 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 3538: 0; >= 3539: -0.16 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.24, 95% band [-0.39, -0.05]).
- `EDUCATION`: education (1 graduate school, 2 university, 3 high school, 4 others; 0, 5 and 6 are not in the data dictionary).
  Share of importance 2.6% (95% band 0.5% to 3.1%); rank 5 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 1: -0.1; >= 2: +0.04 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.14, 95% band [+0.03, +0.17]).
- `AGE`: age in years.
  Share of importance 2.3% (95% band 1.5% to 4.9%); rank 5 to 8 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): rises by 0.17 (95% band [+0.06, +0.35]) from x = 23 (5th percentile) to x = 53 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `BILL_AMT2`: amount of the bill statement in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 2.2% (95% band 0.1% to 5.0%); rank 5 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.20, 95% band [-0.02, +0.38]).
- `PAY_AMT3`: amount paid in July 2005, two months before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 0.2% (95% band 0.0% to 1.8%); rank 7 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.02, 95% band [-0.09, +0.15]).

Interactions: the model has 33 pairs. The larger ones:
- `BILL_AMT1 & AGE`: share of importance 1.6% (95% band 0.0% to 3.1%).
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 201,000: +0.74 (95% band +0.31 to +1.07) when `AGE` = 23, +0.42 (95% band +0.17 to +0.65) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.28 (95% band +0.08 to +0.53) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, -0.05 (95% band -0.30 to +0.20) when `BILL_AMT1` = 201,000.
- `PAY_0 & LIMIT_BAL`: share of importance 1.6% (95% band 1.2% to 3.0%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.26 (95% band +2.09 to +2.61) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, +2.35 (95% band +2.25 to +2.77) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 430,000.
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 430,000: -1.24 (95% band -1.45 to -0.88) when `PAY_0` = -2, -1.15 (95% band -1.39 to -0.70) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `PAY_0 & AGE`: share of importance 1.3% (95% band 0.1% to 2.0%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.52 (95% band +2.37 to +2.70) when `AGE` = 23, +2.50 (95% band +2.42 to +2.80) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.25 (95% band +0.06 to +0.40) when `PAY_0` = -2, +0.23 (95% band +0.06 to +0.53) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `PAY_AMT2 & AGE`: share of importance 1.3% (95% band 0.1% to 1.6%).
  Effect of `PAY_AMT2` from 0 to 19,000: -0.17 (95% band -0.36 to -0.04) when `AGE` = 23, -0.29 (95% band -0.51 to -0.08) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.23 (95% band +0.08 to +0.37) when `PAY_AMT2` = 0, +0.12 (95% band +0.02 to +0.34) when `PAY_AMT2` = 19,000.
- `PAY_0 & BILL_AMT1`: share of importance 1.2% (95% band 0.6% to 2.3%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.22 (95% band +2.05 to +2.51) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, +2.48 (95% band +2.30 to +2.74) when `BILL_AMT1` = 201,000.
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 201,000: +0.48 (95% band +0.07 to +0.75) when `PAY_0` = -2, +0.74 (95% band +0.41 to +0.93) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `PAY_0 & EDUCATION`: share of importance 1.0% (95% band 0.3% to 1.9%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.39 (95% band +2.27 to +2.63) when `EDUCATION` = 1, +2.66 (95% band +2.47 to +2.98) when `EDUCATION` = 3.
  Effect of `EDUCATION` from 1 to 3: +0.12 (95% band +0.00 to +0.21) when `PAY_0` = -2, +0.40 (95% band +0.12 to +0.60) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `LIMIT_BAL & PAY_AMT1`: share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.3% to 1.8%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 430,000: -1.03 (95% band -1.26 to -0.74) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, -1.18 (95% band -1.42 to -0.80) when `PAY_AMT1` = 18,400.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 18,400: -0.49 (95% band -0.75 to -0.18) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, -0.64 (95% band -0.79 to -0.35) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 430,000.
- `LIMIT_BAL & AGE`: share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.2% to 1.6%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 430,000: -1.06 (95% band -1.28 to -0.75) when `AGE` = 23, -1.25 (95% band -1.52 to -0.89) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.32 (95% band +0.10 to +0.52) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, +0.13 (95% band -0.08 to +0.36) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 430,000.
- `PAY_AMT1 & BILL_AMT2`: share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.0% to 1.4%).
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 18,400: -0.54 (95% band -0.81 to -0.26) when `BILL_AMT2` = 0, -0.70 (95% band -0.96 to -0.36) when `BILL_AMT2` = 195,000.
  Effect of `BILL_AMT2` from 0 to 195,000: +0.35 (95% band +0.00 to +0.57) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, +0.18 (95% band -0.11 to +0.50) when `PAY_AMT1` = 18,400.
- `BILL_AMT1 & PAY_AMT2`: share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.1% to 1.2%).
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 201,000: +0.56 (95% band +0.27 to +0.81) when `PAY_AMT2` = 0, +0.67 (95% band +0.29 to +0.87) when `PAY_AMT2` = 19,000.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT2` from 0 to 19,000: -0.27 (95% band -0.43 to -0.07) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, -0.17 (95% band -0.42 to -0.04) when `BILL_AMT1` = 201,000.
- `PAY_AMT1 & AGE`: share of importance 0.7% (95% band 0.0% to 2.0%).
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 18,400: -0.54 (95% band -0.66 to -0.30) when `AGE` = 23, -0.68 (95% band -0.77 to -0.33) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.21 (95% band +0.08 to +0.40) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, +0.07 (95% band -0.03 to +0.36) when `PAY_AMT1` = 18,400.
- `LIMIT_BAL & PAY_AMT2`: share of importance 0.7% (95% band 0.2% to 1.6%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 430,000: -1.20 (95% band -1.48 to -0.86) when `PAY_AMT2` = 0, -1.08 (95% band -1.30 to -0.75) when `PAY_AMT2` = 19,000.

content.text: {"sentences":[{"id":1,"text":"The model's predictions of default are driven mainly by the most recent repayment status (PAY_0), which accounts for about 35% of its importance: applicants who were paid in full or on time look lower risk, while those with payment delays of two months or more look much higher risk."},{"id":2,"text":"The size of the credit limit (LIMIT_BAL) is the second most important driver, at about 19%: larger limits are associated with lower predicted default risk, and this effect is fairly consistent across the range."},{"id":3,"text":"The amount paid in the latest month (PAY_AMT1) and the latest bill amount (BILL_AMT1) matter less, at about 9% and 8%; larger payments lower predicted risk, while larger bills raise it, though the bill effect is less certain given its wide uncertainty band."},{"id":4,"text":"Payment amounts from August (PAY_AMT2) have a smaller, modest downward effect, while education, age and the August bill amount contribute only small effects whose uncertainty ranges are wide enough that the data do not firmly establish their direction or size."},{"id":5,"text":"The effect of repayment status is strongest for the largest delays and is somewhat stronger for applicants with lower credit limits and for those with higher bills, though these interactions are modest compared with the main effect."},{"id":6,"text":"The effect of credit limit is reduced for applicants with recent payment delays, since the risk-lowering effect of a higher limit is weaker when PAY_0 is high, and the interaction with age and payments is small."},{"id":7,"text":"The third-month-earlier payment amount (PAY_AMT3) has essentially no measurable effect on predictions, so it can be disregarded in interpreting this model."}]}
